newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES may issue convertible bond on five pct shares.
newsitem.headline: UES may issue convertible bond on five pct shares.

text.p: Russian national electric company UES is considering a few variations for a convertible bond programme to begin this autumn and bonds could be issued on up to five percent of shares, a senior official said on Friday.

"Five percent is one of the possibilities," said investor relations administration head Pavel Shabanov, adding that bonds could cover 2.7 percent of company shares held by the government and 2.3 percent of company shares which have been authorised but not issued.
Shabanov said a government order being prepared would clarify the matter.
A government programme approving the concept of issuing convertible bonds holds that the government will maintain a controlling stake in UES, at least 50 percent plus one share, he said.

He said two other possibilities for the scheme were to issue the interest-bearing bonds, with what he said was a minimum three-year conversion maturity, on 1.7 percent or 2.7 percent of company shares in government hands.

Unified Energy System's chief executive Boris Brevnov said on Thursday the bonds would be issued in tranches but it was not clear what part of the proceeds would go to badly-needed company infrastructure rebuilding and what to the state.
